subject: Numeracy
title: Sorting by colour
subtopics: Saying the colour of a group
objectives: Children will put objects of the same colour together.
Children will name or point to a group by its colour.
content: Sorting familiar objects into groups by colour and saying the colour of a group.
teachingActivities: Model sorting aloud ("red goes here"); give each child a basket and a sorting cloth; praise careful sorting; ask "Why does it go here?"
learnerActivities: Pick up, sort and place objects of one colour together, name the colour or point to it, and tidy sorted objects away.
resources: Coloured cloths or paper plates (red, yellow, green)
Large safe objects in red, yellow and green (tomato, plantain, leaf, plastic cups)
assessment: Note whether each child sorts without errors, whether they name a colour, and whether they need prompts.
expectedOutcomes: Sorts into two colour groups with few errors.
Names at least one colour in a group.
crossCurricular: Science: noticing the colour of fruits and leaves

lessons.title: Red things go here
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will put red objects in one place and non-red objects in another.
successCriteria: Places a red object in the red basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match identical objects and sometimes say same or different.
resources: Four red objects (red cup, red ball, red cloth, tomato) and four non-red objects
lessons.starter: Show a red tomato and say "Red tomato. Red!" Put on a red hat or hold a red cloth. Tell the children "Today we will find red things."
teacherActivities: Put the red cloth on the mat. Pick up a red cup and say "Red cup goes on the red cloth."
Hold up a blue block and say "Blue block. Does it go on red? No." Put it aside.
Invite each child to choose one object and decide whether it goes on the red cloth.
learnerActivities: Children shake their heads or say "no".
Child chooses an object and puts it on the red cloth if it is red.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the red cloth on the mat. Pick up a red cup and say "Red cup goes on the red cloth." Children: Children watch, then say "red".
Step 2. Teacher: Hold up a blue block and say "Blue block. Does it go on red? No." Put it aside. Children: Children shake their heads or say "no".
Step 3. Teacher: Invite each child to choose one object and decide whether it goes on the red cloth. Children: Child chooses an object and puts it on the red cloth if it is red.

practical.title: Find the reds
steps: Spread eight objects on the mat.
Children take turns to put a red object in the red basket.
Ask the class to check by pointing and saying "red".
practical.safety: Use only large objects that cannot be swallowed. A tomato should be firm and washed; do not let children eat it during the activity.

differentiation.support: Use only red and blue objects and guide the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a red thing in the room that is not on the mat.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which one is red?
questions.expected: Child points to a red object.

questions.question: Does the blue block go here?

lessons.conclusion: Count how many red things are in the basket by pointing, without worrying about number. Say "All red! Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: At home, look for red objects such as a cup, a tomato or a cloth and say "red".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put red objects in one place and non-red objects in another" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Red, red, red. Find the red. Red, red, red. Put it in the basket.

lessons.title: Red and yellow baskets
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort objects into a red basket and a yellow basket.
successCriteria: Places objects in the correct colour basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match identical objects and sometimes say same or different.
resources: A red and a yellow basket
Six red and six yellow objects (plastic cups, large blocks, cloths, ripe plantain toy)
lessons.starter: Hold up a yellow plantain (or toy) and a red tomato. Say "Yellow plantain, red tomato." Ask "Which one is yellow?"
teacherActivities: Place the two baskets side by side. Put one red and one yellow object in the correct baskets while thinking aloud.
Hand out one object to each child.
Pick up a mistake on purpose and ask "Is this right?"
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the colour names with you.
Child decides which basket it belongs in and puts it there.
Children say "no" and move it to the correct basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place the two baskets side by side. Put one red and one yellow object in the correct baskets while thinking aloud. Children: Children watch and say the colour names with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Hand out one object to each child. Children: Child decides which basket it belongs in and puts it there.
Step 3. Teacher: Pick up a mistake on purpose and ask "Is this right?" Children: Children say "no" and move it to the correct basket.

practical.title: Two-basket sort
steps: Children sit around a tray of mixed red and yellow objects.
They take turns to sort one at a time.
The class checks each basket and says the colour.
practical.safety: Use blocks and cups larger than a child’s fist. Supervise to prevent mouthing.

differentiation.support: Use only one object at a time and say the colour before the child places it.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count how many are in each basket by touching and say "more" or "same".

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Where does the yellow cup go?
What colour is this basket?
questions.expected: Red or yellow depending on the basket.

lessons.conclusion: Look at the two full baskets and say "Red basket, yellow basket." Tidy by carrying them to the shelf.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort fruit in a bowl: red tomatoes and yellow plantains or lemons. Talk about the colours.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort objects into a red basket and a yellow basket" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Three colour sort
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort objects into three colour groups with help.
successCriteria: Places most objects in the correct group
Names or points to a colour on request
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match identical objects and sometimes say same or different.
resources: Nine objects in these colours (leaf, cloth, cup, block)
lessons.starter: Sing a rainbow song with the colours red, yellow and green. Show each plate and say the colour.
teacherActivities: Introduce the green plate with a leaf. Say "Green leaf goes on the green plate."
Give each child one object and ask them to find its plate.
Ask "Which plate has the most?" in a simple way, pointing to piles.
learnerActivities: Children touch the leaf and say "green".
Child puts the object on the matching plate.
Children point to the biggest pile.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Introduce the green plate with a leaf. Say "Green leaf goes on the green plate." Children: Children touch the leaf and say "green".
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child one object and ask them to find its plate. Children: Child puts the object on the matching plate.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which plate has the most?" in a simple way, pointing to piles. Children: Children point to the biggest pile.

practical.title: Plate sort
steps: Place three plates in a row.
Children take turns to take an object from a bag.
They place it on the matching plate and name the colour.
practical.safety: Use leaves that are clean and non-toxic or use paper leaves. Make sure all objects are too big to swallow.

differentiation.support: Keep to two colours and only two objects in each pile.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another green thing in the classroom.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Show me the yellow plate.
questions.expected: Child points to the yellow plate.

expectedOutcomes: Names or points to red, yellow and green
lessons.conclusion: Sing the colour song and let each child place one object back in the bag.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for red, yellow and green foods at home and name each colour.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort objects into three colour groups with help" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Colour walk
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Saying the colour of a group
objectives: Children will find and sort colourful objects outdoors.
successCriteria: Collects an object of a named colour
Names the colour of their collection
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match identical objects and sometimes say same or different.
resources: A safe outdoor area or a covered corridor
lessons.starter: Show the colour cards and say "Today we are going on a colour walk! Can you find something green?"
teacherActivities: Walk with the children to a safe outdoor area. Name each colour card as you hold it up.
Let each child collect one leaf, flower petal or fallen item of the colour you name.
Ask each child to name the colour of their item.
learnerActivities: Children look around and point to things of that colour.
Child brings the item and places it in the correct basket.
Child says the colour or points to a card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk with the children to a safe outdoor area. Name each colour card as you hold it up. Children: Children look around and point to things of that colour.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child collect one leaf, flower petal or fallen item of the colour you name. Children: Child brings the item and places it in the correct basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask each child to name the colour of their item. Children: Child says the colour or points to a card.

practical.title: Colour treasure hunt
steps: Give each child a colour card.
They find an object that matches the card.
They bring it to the basket and say the colour.
practical.safety: Keep the walk within a fenced area. Do not pick unknown plants and keep hands out of mouths. Wash hands after outdoor collecting.

differentiation.support: Walk beside the child and point to a suitable object.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find something that is two colours.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which basket does it go in?

expectedOutcomes: Finds and names a colour outdoors
lessons.conclusion: Empty the baskets together and say "Red, yellow, green. Well done!" Wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: On the way home or at the market, spot something red, yellow and green.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find and sort colourful objects outdoors" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Colour sorting stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Saying the colour of a group
objectives: Children will show they can sort by colour at three stations.
successCriteria: Sorts correctly into two or three groups
Names or points to a colour
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match identical objects and sometimes say same or different.
lessons.starter: Sing the colour song and show the stations. Remind children to sort carefully.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask each observed child to sort four objects and name one colour.
Note each child’s level and take a photograph.
learnerActivities: Child sorts and names a colour.
Children tidy their station when the signal sounds.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children sort at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask each observed child to sort four objects and name one colour. Children: Child sorts and names a colour.
Step 3. Teacher: Note each child’s level and take a photograph. Children: Children tidy their station when the signal sounds.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Remove any small items and keep all objects larger than a child’s fist.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner at the station.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sort a mixed basket into three groups without help.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sorts objects by colour; names or points to colours.

questions.question: Where does the green one go?
questions.expected: On the green plate or in the green basket.

questions.question: What colour is this?
questions.expected: The correct colour name or a pointing response.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
Sorts by colour with growing accuracy
lessons.conclusion: Sing the colour song and tidy the baskets together.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort toys or fruit by colour with your child this week.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can sort by colour at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
